ranking.note: Raised to P1: a data race on the live block template in the IPC mining path (issue #36515) can corrupt reads or crash the node for the interface's current consumers — a reliability consequence, not merely a feature.

Raised to P1: it introduces BlockTemplateManager, the base that #36356, #36357 and the template-memory accounting in #33922 build on, and removes per-tick cs_main acquisition and full block assembly in waitNext.

Placed ahead of its score position because it is the only PR here fixing a bug miners actually hit today (spurious 'Internal bug detected' on longpoll during shutdown, issue #34262), ahead of tooling and refactors.

Moved up from position 16: signed-overflow UB in cluster-mempool fee arithmetic that silently drops prioritised transactions from templates outranks tooling and refactor work, even if the trigger is unrealistic.
Lowered to P4: reviewers confirm the no-mempool lookup path is unreachable in production, making this a narrow contract-consistency fix next to the real bug fixes kept at P3.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain: #35581 introduces BlockTemplateManager, #36356 moves the getblocktemplate cache into it, and #36357 is explicitly based on #36356. Review in that order; #36357 cannot land first.
#33922 (getMemoryLoad / template memory accounting) also builds on BlockTemplateManager state, so it is downstream of #35581 even though both are high in this list.
#35598 is test coverage extracted from #33922; reviewing #33922 first makes the test's purpose clear, but the test is mergeable independently.

#36525 and #35581 both restructure ownership/locking of the active block template (mutex on m_block_template vs. moving template handling into the manager); whoever reviews one should check for overlap or conflicting designs with the other. #36525 should go first since it fixes a live race.
#36367 is labelled mempool but its stated harm is getblocktemplate omitting prioritised transactions; it is ranked here on that template-validity effect only.
result.notes: The list splits cleanly: two PRs with correctness/foundation consequences (a data race and the BlockTemplateManager base), three substantive IPC interface capabilities for external (Stratum v2) consumers, a long tail of small bug fixes, refactors with stated payoffs, and test-only work. Per the category guidance, #36156's exact-limit underfill was kept low because the fee upside is a tiny fraction of a block.
